title: Enterprise Class Modular Cache Hierarchy
problem: Enterprise mission-critical workloads demand cache hierarchies that deliver consistent low-latency performance at sustained processor utilization above 90% across diverse and highly virtualized workloads, while remaining extensible across processor generations and new technology insertions.
motivation: Traditional monolithic cache designs cannot scale across future technology nodes and platform generations without redesign, creating a growing gap between cache hierarchy rigidity and the evolving demands of enterprise and emerging AI workloads.
method: IBM's Telum and Telum II processors use a modular cache design that splits memory into independent slices spread across separate chiplets, connected by high-bandwidth internal pathways. The design includes an adaptive algorithm that learns which cache levels should hold frequently-accessed data during different workload phases, automatically adjusting as access patterns change. The approach shows how memory requests flow through these cache levels and how changing cache sizes impacts overall performance. This design allows Telum II to simultaneously handle both traditional enterprise business workloads and generative AI inference tasks.
key_novelty: IBM's Telum processors achieve 90%+ sustained processor utilization in enterprise and generative AI workloads by combining a modular, distributed cache architecture with an algorithm that adapts which cache levels hold the most frequently-accessed data.
contributions: Novel modular, scalable cache hierarchy architecture extendable across IBM Z platform generations
Adaptive horizontal cache persistence algorithm that dynamically tunes data retention across cache levels
Performance characterization of cache size sensitivity in enterprise workload contexts
Integration of generative AI capability into mission-critical IBM Telum II design without compromising enterprise SLAs

metrics.other: Sustained processor utilization >90%; specific speedup numbers not disclosed in abstract

limitations: Implementation details and quantitative performance data are not fully disclosed, limiting external reproducibility.
primary_theme: Modular enterprise cache hierarchy for mission-critical and AI workloads
